summary: On paper this one is close: Cincinnati's best edge is to win through the air (Cincinnati ranks 8th in EPA per dropback, +0.20), while Baltimore's best counter is to win short yardage (Baltimore's defense ranks 4th in short-yardage run success, 53% allowed). Under center, Joe Burrow ranks 8th of 26 in EPA per dropback; x-factor: Tee Higgins gets 23% of Cincinnati's targets and 39% of its air yards, and Baltimore's pass defense ranks 15th. The model favors Cincinnati at 52%, mostly on starting QB (1.8 pts) and defensive injuries (1.1 pts).
